The electromagnetic inverse medium scattering problem is governed by the time-harmonic Maxwell equations: curl curl E(r) - κ²(1-a(r))E(r) = 0 in R³
The wave number is defined as κ = √(ε₀μ₀)ω where ω is angular frequency, ε₀ is electric permittivity, and μ₀ is magnetic permeability of vacuum
The refractive index n(r) = √(1-a(r)) is assumed to be C^{1,α}-smooth, real, positive, and supported in the unit ball B = {r ∈ R³ : |r| < 1}
The forward scattering problem uses an equivalent formulation via the electromagnetic Lippmann-Schwinger equation with scalar fundamental solution Φ(r) = exp(iκ|r|)/(4π|r|)
The scattered field E^s must satisfy the Silver-Müller radiation condition ensuring outgoing wave behavior at infinity
The inverse problem reconstructs the refractive index from measurements of the far field pattern E^∞(r̂;d,p) for all r̂,d ∈ S² and polarizations p ∈ C³ with d·p = 0
The regularization parameter schedule γ_k = γ₀γ^{-k} with γ > 1 ensures exponential decay during Newton iterations
The normal equations at each Newton iteration have the form G_k^T G_k h_k = G_k^T g_k where G_k = [A_k; √γ_k I] and g_k = [y^obs - F(x_k); √γ_k b_k]
For exponentially ill-posed problems, the eigenvalues λ₁ ≥ ... ≥ λ_M of A_k^T A_k decay at an exponential rate
The spectrum of the preconditioned matrix M^{-1}G_k^T G_k has eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity #J and other eigenvalues 1 + λ_j/γ_k for j ∉ J
Lanczos' method approximates at most one Ritz pair for multiple isolated eigenvalues, necessitating preconditioner updates
The preconditioner is recomputed when k+1 ≥ √(m+1) + 1, generalizing the rule to recompute at perfect squares
The preconditioner is updated when the last update is at least 4 Newton steps ago and the previous step had more than 5 inner CG iterations
For random noise with covariance Cov_ε, the propagated error estimate is Φ(k) = √(trace(R_k^T Cov_ε R_k)) where R_k = (G_k^T G_k)^{-1} A_k
The Lepski-type stopping rule parameter is set to ρ = 4.1 in numerical experiments with K_max = max{k ∈ ℕ : Φ(k) ≤ R}
The numerical experiments use 25 incident waves with random directions and polarizations drawn from uniform distributions on S²
The data vector has size N = 2·25·100 = 5000 from 25 incident waves and 100 measurement directions
The unknown perturbation a is represented by M coefficients where 500 ≤ M ≤ 2000 using tensor products of splines in radial direction and spherical harmonics in angular direction
The forward problem discretization uses 3·32³ = 98,304 to 3·64³ = 786,432 degrees of freedom for representing E(·;d,p)
The fast solver for the Lippmann-Schwinger equation converges super-linearly for smooth refractive indices
The paper assumes injectivity of the continuous Fréchet derivative F'[x] can be shown for the electromagnetic medium scattering problem by modifying uniqueness proofs
Ritz values are selected for the preconditioner only if sufficiently well separated from the cluster at 1, specifically ≥ 1.1
The paper uses Newton-CG in the initial phase when updates h_k are large, as keeping the Jacobian frozen is inefficient early on
Complete reorthogonalization in Algorithm 1 uses Householder transformations to maintain numerical stability
The stopping criterion in Algorithm 1 is ||r_l|| > εγ_k||h_l|| ensuring relative accuracy of ε/(1-ε) when ||(G_k^T G_k)^{-1}|| ≤ 1/γ_k
